As Apple continues to expand its car key feature across the automotive industry, the functionality now appears to be coming to select models from a major Chinese automaker. Details below.

Apple Wallet's car key feature is reportedly set to support GWM Tank models

New backend code discovered by MacRumors suggests Apple may soon extend the Apple Wallet car key feature to GWM (Great Wall Motors) Tank series vehicles.

Several GWM models already support Apple CarPlay, including the Tank 300, Tank 400, Tank 500 and Tank 700, as well as vehicles from its Haval, Ora, Wey and Cannon brands.

However, none of these models currently support the car key feature, which allows drivers to use an iPhone or Apple Watch to lock, unlock and start a paired vehicle.

Just days before this news broke, new backend code indicated that the car key feature would be coming to Volkswagen models. Following earlier rollouts on brands such as Toyota and Rivian, Apple has been steadily expanding its support for the feature.

Apple previously announced in 2025 that 13 automotive brands would be added to the car key feature's supported lineup, including GWM's Wey brand, as well as Acura, Cadillac, Chery, Chevrolet, GMC, Hongqi, Lucid, Porsche, Rivian, Smart, Tata Motors and Voyah.

According to Apple's official website, more than 800 vehicle models currently support CarPlay, of which 52 also support the car key feature. Click here to view the full compatibility list.
